pages.Pans:
<templatestyles src="Template:Stat/styles.css" />

'''Pans''' are one of the key tools used by the player in ''Prospecting!''  They are vital for progression.

They can typically be found near [[Shopkeepers]], alongside their [[Shovels|shovel]] counterparts.

'''Pans''' have [[Stats|four core stats]]: {{Stat|Luck}}, {{Stat|Capacity}}, {{Stat|Shake Strength}}, and {{Stat|Shake Speed}}. Some pans also include unique passive stats or abilities.

You can [[Enchanting|enchant]] your pans and/or add [[Trinkets|Trinkets]] to them for extra perks.

You can change your equipped pan using the [[Prospector Kit]].

'''Minerals''' can be obtained by prospecting, and can later be sold at a [[Merchant]]. Minerals come in different rarities, and are found in different deposits. Every Mineral found by the player gets documented in the "Collection" item, which is part of the gear you get when first joining the game.

== Modifiers ==
See also: [[Modifiers]] - special effects that can change the value of minerals.

'''Shovels''' are one of the key tools used by the player in ''Prospecting!'' and are vital for progression.

They can typically be found near [[Shopkeepers]], alongside their [[Pans|pan]] counterparts.

'''Shovels''' have three main [[Stats|stats]]: {{Stat|Dig Strength}}, {{Stat|Dig Speed}}, and {{Stat|Toughness}}.

You can [[Enchanting#tabber-Shovels|enchant]] your shovel to give it extra abilities.

Use your [[Prospector Kit]] to change your equipped shovel.

'''Sluices''' are automated devices that sift valuables from running water in ''Prospecting!''. Great for passive income and progression. They can be placed in flowing water to collect while you explore or are offline. '''Sluices''' have [[Stats|four core stats]]: {{Stat|Luck}}, {{Stat|Capacity}}, {{Stat|Efficiency}}, and {{Stat|Toughness}}. Many sluices can be upgraded by talking to the [[Mad Scientist]] in the small workshop near the {{Crystal Caverns}} [[Waypoints|waypoint]]. pages.Enchanting:
== Enchanting == ''Notes'' * Enchants apply '''only''' to your currently equipped [[Pans|pan]] and [[Shovels|shovel]]. Max '''1''' enchant per pan/shovel (you can re-enchant anytime). == Available Enchantments == |-| Pans = == How to Enchant == [[File:Fortune Altar.png|thumb|The '''Fortune River Altar''']] * Head over to the Mysterious Altar located behind the Alchemist Store in {{Fortune River}}. * Make sure that the pan you want to enchant is the one you have equipped. * Interact with the altar and choose "Enchant my pan". * Click an ore ([[Aurorite]], [[Aetherite]], or [[Aetherium]]) on the left side. Enchanting will happen immediately! Make sure you don't accidentally click on an ore while scrolling through the list! * The name and stats of the resulting enchant will be shown on the right. If it's not the enchant you wanted, keep clicking ores; otherwise, close the interface. ''Notes'' * As an alternative to taking your chances with the altar, [[Relics#Enchant_Relics|Enchant books]] are available from the [[Traveling Merchant]] and [[Excavations|Excavation Sites]] for some enchant types. * The weight or modifier of the ore does '''not''' affect the rarity of the enchant you might get. {| class="wikitable sortable" style="width:100%;" |+ Available Pan Enchantments ! pages.Stats: {{Tocright}} == Overview == '''Stats''' in '''Prospecting!''' refer to the numerical values that dictate how you obtain and sell [[minerals]], among other things. === '''Stats''' can be affected by === * [[Equipment|Equipment]] * [[Events]] * [[Shovels]] and [[pans]] * [[Enchanting]] * Temporary boosts ** Daily rewards ** Completing certain [[:Category:Quests|Quests]] ** [[Codes]] == List of Stats == {| class="fandom-table" !Stat !Description !Factors |- |'''Dig Strength''' |Dig Strength refers to how much sediment you can add to your pan when digging. |[[Shovels|Shovel]], [[Enchanting]], [[Potions]] |- |'''Dig Speed''' |Dig Speed refers to how fast the bar moves on the perfect dig scale and the time in-between each dig. |[[Enchanting]], [[Potions]] |- |'''Shake Strength''' |Shake Strength refers to how much sediment you remove per click when panning. |[[Pans]], [[Enchanting]], [[Potions]] |- |'''Shake Speed''' |Shake Speed refers to how fast you can click while shaking. |[[Pans]], [[Enchanting]], [[Potions]] |- |'''Capacity (Pans)''' |Capacity (pans) refers to the amount of sediment you can store in your pan. Also affects how many [[minerals]] you can get from one pan cycle (square root of capacity = average minerals) and increases mineral size. |[[Pans]], [[Enchanting]], [[Potions]] |- |'''Capacity (Sluices)''' |Capacity (sluices) refers to the total number of [[minerals]] you can store in a [[Sluices|sluice]]. |[[Sluices]] |- |'''Efficiency (Sluices)''' |Efficiency refers to the amount of minerals a given sluice will accumulate each 10 minutes. |[[Sluices]] |- |'''Luck''' |Luck increases your chances of finding rarer/bigger [[minerals]]. Mechanics can be found [[Luck Mechanics|here]]. |[[Enchanting]], [[Events]], [[Potions]] |- |'''Size Boost''' |Size Boost refers to the multiplier that will affect [[Minerals|mineral]] weights when you pan for them. |[[Enchanting]], [[Events]] |- |'''Modifier Boost''' |Modifier Boost refers to the multiplier that will affect the chance for minerals to have [[Modifiers|modifiers]]. |[[Enchanting]], [[Events]], [[Potions]] |- |'''Sell Boost''' |Sell Boost refers to the multiplier to the amount of money you will receive when selling [[minerals]] and [[Equipment|equipment]] to a [[merchant]]. |[[Enchanting]], [[Events]], [[Potions]] |- |'''Inventory Size''' |Inventory size increases your max inventory space inside of your inventory. So, how many items you can carry. | |- |'''Self-Propulsion (Sluices)''' |Self-Propulsion allows you to put your sluice in non-moving water. (i.e. anywhere except {{The Void}} and the {{Infernal Heart}}) |[[Sluices]] |- |'''Autocollect (Sluices)''' |Autocollect will automatically collect ores from your sluice, '''as long as you are online'''. |[[Sluices]] |- |'''WalkSpeed''' |Determines how fast your character moves across the map. |[[Potions]], [[Runes]], [[Sluices|Easter Sluice]], [[Equipment]] |- |'''Jump Power''' |Determines the height of your character jump height. |[[Equipment]] |- |'''Status Timer Speed''' |Determines how much slower your buffs like potions and the cookie affect last, -50% means twice as long effects. |[[Equipment]] |- |'''Treasure Chest Chance''' |Increases the likelihood of discovering chests during activities. For more details, see the [[Treasure Map]] page. |[[Equipment]] |}

pages.Merchant:
[[File:Merchantfort.png|right|300px]]

The '''Merchant''' is a recurring [[NPCs|NPC]] in ''Prospecting!''.  
They appear in multiple towns and digsites, allowing the player to sell [[Minerals]] and [[Equipment|equipment]] for money.  

Merchants are functionally the same as the [[Shady Merchant]], but are more common and serve as the main way to convert items into cash.

== Gameplay ==
Merchants allow the player to:
* Sell individual items
* Sell all items at once (except those favorited)
* Gain sell boosts through certain effects (see below)

== Locations ==

=== Mainland ===
* {{Rubble Creek}} — near [[John]] and the [[Trader]]  
* {{Fortune River}} — between the [[Kid]] and the [[Shard Merchant]]  
* {{Crystal Caverns}} — next to the [[Head Researcher]] and a [[Shopkeepers|Shopkeeper]]
* {{Sunset Beach}} — next to the shack

=== Caldera Park === 
* {{Volcanic Sands}} — close to the [[Ranger]] and the [[Waypoints|Waypoint]]  
* {{Magma Furnace}} — next to the Dragonflame [[equipment]] 

=== Snowy Mountain ===
* {{Snowy Shores}} — near the {{Frostbite River}} and the [[Researcher]]  
* {{Frostbitten Path}} — at the {{Frostbite Waterfall}}, under a tree  
* {{Frozen Peak}} — close to the [[Mountain Climber]]  

=== Overgrown Caves ===
* {{Overgrown Grotto}} — next to the [[Waypoints|waypoint]]
* {{Enchanted Ruins}} — sitting on a stone wall  

=== Rotwood Swamp ===
* {{Rotwood Swamp}} — in the house to the right of the [[Waypoints|waypoint]]
* {{Timelocked Sanctuary}} — on the left, near the shrine 

=== Meteor Valley ===
* {{Meteor Falls}} — near the [[Familiar Merchant]]
* {{Starfall River}} — across the river from the [[Astronomer]]   
* {{Astral Caverns}} — near the [[Alchemist|Alchemist's]] shop   

== Sell Boosts ==
Players can increase their sell rate temporarily or permanently:  
* '''Merchant’s Potion''' — bought from the [[Shard Merchant]] for {{Meteor Shards|200}} 
* [[Permanent_Buffs#Trader's_Recommendation|Trader's Recommendation (permanent buff)]]  
* Certain [[Codes]]  
* Putting {{Stat|Sell Boost}} ores in the [[Museum]]
* Some [[Equipment]]
* {{XP Cookie}}

[[File:Prospector_Kit_Equipment_Equip.png|100px|thumb|The stat popup for a necklace in the Prospector Kit]] There are three types of equipment (jewelry) in the game: Necklaces, Charms, and Rings. You can wear one necklace and one charm, and up to 8 rings. Use the [[Prospector Kit]] to equip and unequip your jewelry, and/or to save or load a particular arrangement ("loadout"). Equipment can be crafted at the [[Crafting Anvil]] near the [[Blacksmith]] in multiple locations. Some equipment needs a [[Blueprint]] to be obtained before it can be crafted, while other equipment can be crafted by all players, provided they have the ingredients. Equipment can be [[Crafting_Anvil#Quality|improved]] in multiple ways. * When crafting, use larger/better ores to get more stars. * Ask the Blacksmith to '''reforge''' the equipment. This has a chance (though not a guarantee unless you use a [[Perfect Reforge Token]] or pay the Blacksmith with Robux) to raise the percentage score. * Merge two five-star equipment into one six-star equipment at the [[Magma Forge]]. * [[Mutations|Mutate]] the equipment at the forge at {{Frozen Peak}}. == List of Equipment ==  c = Catalyst for [[Mutations]] |-|Common= {| class="wikitable sortable equip-table" style="width:100%" ! = Potions =
'''Potions''' are consumable items in '''Prospecting''' that grant temporary stat boosts when used.  
They can be purchased from various merchants across the world.  

Each potion lasts for a limited time and provides effects such as increased '''Luck''', '''Capacity''', '''Strength''', '''Shake Speed''', and more.  

== Overview ==
Potions can be purchased from the following merchants:
* [[#Fortune River Town Alchemist|Fortune River Town Alchemist]] – basic Luck and Capacity potions  
* [[#Volcanic Sands Alchemist|Volcanic Sands Alchemist]] – powerful Luck and Strength potions  
* [[#Frostbitten Path Alchemist|Frostbitten Path Alchemist]] – more powerful Luck and Speed potions
* [[#Rotwood Swamp Alchemist|Rotwood Swamp Alchemist]] – even more powerful Luck potions
* [[#Astral Caverns Alchemist|Astral Caverns Alchemist]] - luck, strength, and size boost potions
* [[#Desert Alchemist|Desert Alchemist]] - luck, mod boost, and speed potions
* [[#Shard Merchant|Shard Merchant]] – potion focused on sell value  
* [[#Traveling Merchant|Traveling Merchant]] – rare and unique potions  

=== Usage ===
* Potions can be purchased "in bulk" by inputting the desired number.
** If you put in a larger number than the merchant's stock, it will say "out of stock" and no potions will be purchased.
* The potion(s) will go into your inventory (backpack) as a consumable item.
* To use a potion, select it in your inventory, then click/tap on the screen.
* When using the potion, if you have more than one, you can input the desired duration by selecting the number of potions to activate.
** Unlike the purchasing window, the duration window will not let you select more potions than what you have in your inventory.

pages.Museum: {{Tocright}} [[File:Museum.png|thumb|300px|''The Museum'']] = Museum = The '''Museum''' is an indoor [[Locations|location]] in {{Caldera Park}} where players can place minerals into display pedestals to earn permanent stat boosts. Each display accepts minerals of a specific rarity, ranging from '''Common''' to '''Exotic'''. The '''Museum''' also has a [[Vault]] to the right of the [[Receptionist]], as well as a [[Manage Museums Board]] and [[Visit Museums Globe]]. == Staff == * [[Receptionist]] — Quest-giving NPC who manages the Museum. == Extras == * [[Vault]] — Allows players to store extra minerals and materials * [[MVP|Voting box]] — Vote for the next [[MVP]] * [[Manage Museums Board]] — Save different museum setups and quickly switch between them * [[Visit Museums Globe]] — See what other players have in their museums == Displays == [[File:Museum_Display.png|thumb|280px|''A Display Pedestal'']] The Museum contains rarity-based displays. * For '''Common''' through '''Legendary''' rarities, each rarity has '''1 free display''' and '''2 locked displays''', one unlockable with money, the other with [[Meteor Shards]]. * For the '''Mythic''' rarity, there are only 2 displays (money + shards, no free). * The '''Exotic''' rarity has only 1 display (shards only). {| class="wikitable" style="width:100%; text-align:center;" ! Rarity !! Free Displays !! Locked Displays !! Price (Money) !! Price (Shards) !! pages.Prospector Kit:
[[File:Prospector Kit hotbar.png]] [[File:Prospector Kit popup.png|150px|thumb|The Prospector Kit is "used to manage your equipment."]] The Prospector Kit is arguably the most important interface in the game. It's where you can equip and unequip your tools ([[Pans|pans]], [[Shovels|shovels]], and [[Sluices|sluices]]) and [[Equipment|equipment]] (rings, charms, and necklaces). The Pans tab is also where you can equip [[Trinkets]], and the Equipment tab is where you can equip [[Runes]]. == Pans == [[File:Prospector Kit Pans.png|400px|thumb|The equipped pan is Pharaoh's Pan with Irregular enchantment and Beach Umbrella trinket]] The pans you own are listed on the left side. If a pan has an [[Enchanting|enchantment]] applied, it is shown before the name of the pan. The currently-selected pan is shown on the right side, along with its description and [[Stats]]. [[File:Prospector Kit Pan Enchant Stats.png|200px|none]] The effects of the enchantment (if any) are shown after the pan's base stats, in a color that matches the enchantment's name. If the selected pan is currently equipped, the button at the bottom will say "[Equipped]"; otherwise, the button will say "Equip", and clicking it will change your pan to the new selection. You cannot unequip all pans; you can only switch between them. The button below the right side shows the [[Trinkets|trinket]] applied to the selected pan, if any. Click the button to change the trinket. == Shovels == [[File:Prospector Kit Shovels.png|400px|thumb|The selected (but not equipped) shovel is a Mastered-enchanted Starcrusher.]] The shovels you own are listed on the left side. If a shovel has an [[Enchanting|enchantment]] applied, it is shown before the name of the shovel. The currently-selected shovel is shown on the right side, along with its description and [[Stats]]. The effects of the enchantment (if any) are shown below the shovel's description, in a color that matches the enchantment's name. If the selected shovel is currently equipped, the button at the bottom will say "[Equipped]"; otherwise, the button will say "Equip", and clicking it will change your shovel to the new selection. As with pans, it is not possible to unequip all shovels; you can only switch between them. == Sluices == [[File:Prospector Kit Sluices.png|400px|thumb|The Pharaoh's Sluice with 35 upgrade points applied]] The sluices you own are listed on the left side. If a sluice has been [[Sluices#tabber-Sluice_Upgrades_(Crystal_Caverns)|upgraded]], the number of upgrade points is listed in parentheses after the sluice name. The currently-selected sluice is shown on the right side, along with its description and [[Stats]]. If a stat has been upgraded, the amount added will be listed in parentheses after the base number. Note that only the four numeric stats are listed — Autocollect and Self-Propulsion are not shown in the Prospector Kit. === Equipping and Unequipping === * If the selected sluice is currently equipped, the button at the bottom will say "Unequip". Clicking the button will remove the sluice from your hotbar (as well as the body of water it was in, if any). * If the selected sluice is not the one currently equipped, the button at the bottom will say "Equip". Clicking the button will change your hotbar button to the new sluice, or if you didn't have a sluice equipped previously, it will add a button. ** If there's no room on your hotbar, the sluice will be put in your backpack, but next time you rejoin, it will almost certainly scramble your hotbar to make room for the sluice. == Equipment == [[File:Prospector Kit Equipment.png|400px|thumb|A luck-efficiency equipment loadout]] The left side of the screen has two parts: on the top is a list of your available equipment (in pretty much random order), and on the bottom is a list of your saved loadouts (again, in random order, though at least it doesn't move them around once saved). The right side of the screen shows the equipment slots available and what you're wearing in them. It also has a button for selecting your [[Runes]]. If you have yet to purchase a ring slot, its price (in {{Meteor Shards|Meteor Shards}}) will be shown; click the slot to buy it. The last two ring slots can be purchased in the [[Prospector's_Shop#Passes|Prospector's Shop]] (for Robux). === Equipping and Unequipping ===
[[File:Prospector Kit Equipment Unequip.png|100px|left]] To unequip something you're currently wearing, click or tap on it on the right side of the screen.
[[File:Prospector Kit Equipment Equip.png|100px|left]] * To equip something, first make sure there's an empty slot for it, then click or tap it on the left side of the screen. ** Alternatively, close the Prospector Kit, find the item in your backpack, select it, then "use" it by clicking on the screen.
=== Loadouts === The game will let you save up to 10 named sets of equipment, called a "loadout". Unlike [[Museum]] ores, you can use your equipment in as many loadouts as you wish. ;Saving a new loadout # Equip the desired arrangement of necklaces, charms, and rings on the right side of your screen. # Click the "Save As"[ahem, sorry] "New+" button. # Type in a name for the loadout, then click the Confirm button. ;Using a loadout # Click the name of the loadout in the list on the left. # There is no step 2. ;Deleting a loadout # Click the trashcan icon next to the name of the loadout. # Click Yes to confirm. ;Editing a loadout # Click the name of the loadout you want to change. # Make the desired changes (see [[#Equipping_and_Unequipping_2|Equipping and Unequipping]] above). # Delete the existing loadout name. # Save the new loadout.

pages.Fortune River:
{{Tocright}}


= Fortune River =
'''Fortune River''' is the second major [[Locations|location]] on the [[Mainland]].  
It has one digging site: the '''Fortune River Digsite'''.

== Main Town ==
[[File:Town.png|center|600px|''Main Area'']]
=== Store ===
This is the second store you can visit. It sells four [[Pans|pans]] and four [[Shovels|shovels]].

{| style="width:100%; background: none; border-collapse: collapse;"
| [[File:Town_Store.png|center|300px|''The Store'']]
| style="background: transparent;" |
; Pans
* [[Golden Pan]] — {{$|333,000}}
* [[Magnetic Pan]] — {{$|1,000,000}}
* [[Meteoric Pan]] — {{$|3,500,000}}
* [[Diamond Pan]] — {{$|10,000,000}}

; Shovels
* [[The Excavator]] — {{$|320,000}}
* [[Golden Shovel]] — {{$|1,333,000}}
* [[Meteoric Shovel]] — {{$|4,000,000}}
* [[Diamond Shovel]] — {{$|12,500,000}}
|}

[[File:Shard_Shop.png|thumb|200px|''The Shard Shop'']]  
The [[Shard Merchant]] sells special items for [[Meteor Shards]].

; Totems
* Strength Totem — {{Meteor Shards|180}}
* Luck Totem — {{Meteor Shards|300}}

; Potion
* Merchant's Potion — {{Meteor Shards|200}}

=== Alchemist Store ===
[[File:Alchemist_Shop.png|thumb|200px|''The Alchemist's Store'']]  
The [[Alchemist]] sells four potions that grant temporary stat boosts.  
Greater Potions give double the boost and duration of Basic ones.

; Basic Potions
* Luck Potion — {{$|50,000}}
* Capacity Potion — {{$|40,000}}

; Greater Potions
* Luck Potion — {{Meteor Shards|30}}
* Capacity Potion — {{Meteor Shards|20}}
=== Blacksmith ===
[[File:Blacksmithfort.png|thumb|150px|''The Blacksmith'']]  
The [[Blacksmith]] allows you to [[Equipment|craft]] new equipment and [[Blacksmith|reforge]] existing gear.

=== Enchanting ===
[[File:Enchant_Area.png|thumb|200px|''The Mysterious Altar'']]  
The Mysterious Altar lets you use [[Aurorite]], [[Aetherite]], or [[Aetherium]] to [[Enchanting|enchant]] your pan, giving it a permanent boost.

The [[Archaeologist]] offers a quest related to this feature.

=== Void Portal ===
[[File:Void_Portal.png|thumb|200px|''The Void Portal'']]  
The Void Portal appears at the outskirts of Fortune River Town. {{The Void}} is a mysterious location that appears as a rift in reality.

=== Other NPCs & Utilities ===
* [[Waypoints|Waypoint]] — fast travel between locations
* [[Merchant]] — sell [[Minerals|mineral]]s and [[Equipment|equipment]]
* [[Tired Prospector]] — quest-giving NPC at the side of the Store
* [[Engineer]] — quest-giving NPC behind the Store
* [[Steve]] - quest-giving NPC in front of the Store
* [[Fisherman]] — quest-giving NPC at the Fortune River dock
* [[Archaeologist]] — quest-giving NPC at the Enchanting area
* [[Vagrant]] — quest-giving NPC in the shed
* [[MVP|MVP Voting box]]
* [[Vault]] — extra storage
* [[Dredge Master]] — unlimited quest-giving NPC across the river

=== Extras ===
* '''Kid''' — dislikes the country he lives in
* '''Resident''' — explains Fortune River’s gold abundance
* '''Archaeologist?''' — skeptical NPC who doubts the runes’ purpose

== Digsite ==
[[File:Fortune_River_Digging.png|thumb|200px|''The Fortune River Digsite'']]  
Fortune River's digsite is the third location where a player can dig.  
It requires '''Toughness 3''' (at least a '''Reinforced Shovel''').

pages.Crystal Caverns:

[[File:Crystal Caverns.png|thumb|280px|''Entrance to the Crystal Caverns'']]

= Crystal Caverns =
'''Crystal Caverns''' is a [[Locations|location]] on the [[Mainland]].  
It has one digging site, {{Crystal Cavern River}}, and one sub-area, {{Azuralite Oasis}}.  

== Main Town ==

=== Shop ===
The shop sells one [[Pans|pan]] and one [[Shovels|shovel]].

[[File:Crystal Caverns Shop.png|thumb|280px|''The Shop'']]
'''Pan'''
* Aurora Pan — $35,000,000

'''Shovel'''
* Divine Shovel — $40,000,000

=== Sluice Upgrade Room ===
[[File:SluiceUpgradeDoor.png|thumb|280px|''Door leading to the Sluice Upgrade area'']]  
[[File:SluiceUpgradeRoom.png|thumb|280px|''Inside the Upgrade Room'']]  

The '''Sluice Upgrade Room''' can be accessed through the special door in the {{Crystal Caverns}}.  
Here, players can enhance their [[Sluices|sluices]] by investing resources to improve their stats and efficiency.  

Upgrading your sluice increases its effectiveness, making it possible to yield more valuable [[minerals]] during offline farming.

=== Other NPCs & Utilities ===
* [[Waypoints|Waypoint]] — teleportation between locations  
* [[Merchant]] — allows selling of [[minerals]] and [[Equipment|equipment]]  
* [[Head Researcher]] — quest-giving NPC  
* '''Security Guard''' — prevents players below level 15 from entering  
* '''Scientist''' — researches [[Azuralite]]  
* '''Miner''' — believes mining operations will soon resume  

== Waterfall Temple ==
[[File:Crystal_Caverns_Temple.png|thumb|280px|''Entrance to the Waterfall Temple'']]  
The '''Waterfall Temple''' is hidden behind the waterfall at {{Crystal Cavern River}}.  
To enter, you must sacrifice an [[Emerald]], a [[Diamond]], and a [[Starshine]].  

Inside, there is a shop and one NPC.  

; Shop Items
* Earthbreaker Shovel — $125,000,000  
* Worldshaker Pan — $125,000,000  

; NPC
* [[???]] — grants a [[Permanent Buffs|permanent buff]] of '''+5''' {{stat|Luck}} after dialogue  

== Crystal Cavern River ==
[[File:Crystal_Cavern_Digsite.png|thumb|280px|''The Digsite'']]  
The '''Crystal Cavern River''' is the first digsite in the {{Crystal Caverns}}.  
It requires '''Toughness 4''' (at least a '''Meteoric Shovel''').  
There are '''19''' possible [[minerals]].  

; Minerals
* {{Common}} — [[Silver]], [[Copper]], [[Gold]], [[Amethyst]]  
* {{Uncommon}} — [[Neodymium]], [[Smoky Quartz]], [[Malachite]]  
* {{Rare}} — [[Onyx]], [[Azuralite]]  
* {{Epic}} — [[Ashvein]], [[Emerald]], [[Borealite]], [[Osmium]]  
* {{Legendary}} — [[Palladium]], [[Luminum]], [[Starshine]], [[Aetherite]]  
* {{Mythic}} — [[Inferlume]], [[Vortessence]]  

== Sublocation ==
* The {{Azuralite Oasis}} is a sub-area of the {{Crystal Caverns}}. It requires '''Toughness 5''', and contains the [[Enchanting#tabber-Shovels|shovel enchanting altar]].

= Ancient Ruins =

[[File:Ancient Ruins (Entrance).png|600px|center]]

The '''Ancient Ruins''' are a discoverable landmark located within the {{Windswept Beach}} area.  
They’re referenced on the Windswept Beach entry as “the area where you can find the {{Ancient Ruins}}.”

== Overview ==
A set of weathered structures half-claimed by sand and wind. The site is frequently visited by prospectors exploring {{Windswept Beach}}.

== How to Reach ==
* Found within {{Windswept Beach}}.  
* From the waypoint head towards the lighthouse and complete the quest for the [[Lightkeeper]]. Then go down the lighthouse.
* Nearest fast-travel: see [[Waypoints]].

== NPCs & Services ==
* Nearby NPCs at {{Windswept Beach}}: [[Paleontologist]], [[Merchant]], [[Lightkeeper]].

== Mechanics & Puzzles ==
* To access the ancient ruins you need to open the hatch with a [[Volcanic Key]]. Inside you then need to open the door with 1 [[Catseye]], 1 [[Uranium]] and 1 [[Flarebloom]].

=== Maze Solution ===
* '''Shovel & Pan''' — Left, then right, then left. Interact with the bookshelf in the final room to find the '''Fossilized Shovel''' and '''Fossilized Pan'''.
* '''Sluice''' — Turn right three times. Found among barrels is the '''Fossilized Sluice'''.

</gallery>

= Deeproot Spring =
'''Deeproot Spring''' is a sub-location within {{Overgrown Grotto}}.  

== Services & NPCs ==
* [[Waypoints|Waypoint]] - fast travel between locations
* [[Pans|Pan]]: Lifetouched Pan — $100,000,000,000

== Digsite ==
The spring requires '''Toughness 6'''. There are 21 possible [[Minerals|minerals]].

Talk to the [[Old Druid]] in the {{Overgrown Grotto}} to get the [[Relics#tabber-Enchanted_Scissors|enchanted scissors]], then use the scissors to cut the vines blocking the path to the Spring. = The Abyssal Depths =
'''Abyssal Depths''' is an underground sub-[[Locations|location]] wherein the darkness seems to surround you from every direction. 

Upon entering the Abyss, a purple bar will appear on your screen. To prevent it from filling up, remain close to a [[Firefly Flare]] or Luminant totem. If the bar reaches its maximum, it will result in death.

== Main Area ==

=== Services and NPCs ===
* There is a [[Merchant]] just outside the entrance
* [[Skeleton]] — blueprint-giving NPC  
* [[Firefly Flare|Firefly flare crafting table]] — located just outside the entrance. Firefly flares are consumable items that allow you to stay inside the Abyss without dying.

=== How to Access ===
[[File:Abyss Entrance.png|thumb|250px|''Abyssal Depths Entrance'']]  
[[File:Path Abyssal.png|250px|thumb|''The path that leads to Abyss'']]
* The entrance to Abyssal Depths can be found by going up and around {{Deeproot Spring}} towards the area where you can buy the [[Lifetouched Pan]].
** To enter the depths, jump in the hole.
* There is a ladder that you can set up to easily access the Abyss from the {{Overgrown Grotto}}, without going the long way around Deeproot Spring.
[[File:LadderAbyss.png|250px|center]]

=== How to Exit ===
There is a rope hanging down near the middle of the main area. Climb it to exit the Abyss.

== Digsites ==
[[File:Abyss Main.png|thumb|280px|''The Abyssal Depths digsite'']]  
The digsite of {{Abyssal Depth}} requires '''Toughness 7''' (at least a '''Lifetouched Shovel''').  
There are '''19''' possible [[minerals]].

; Minerals
* {{Common}} — [[Copper]], [[Gold]], [[Silver]]
* {{Uncommon}} — [[Malachite]], [[Neodymium]], [[Smoky Quartz]]
* {{Rare}} — [[Amber]], [[Azuralite]], [[Gloomberry]]
* {{Epic}} — [[Aurorite]], [[Cobalt]], [[Emerald]], [[Lightshard]]
* {{Legendary}} — [[Aetherite]], [[Specterite]], [[Starshine]]
* {{Mythic}} — [[Painite]], [[Radiant Gold]]
* {{Exotic}} — [[Umbrite]]

== The Maze ==
[[File:AbyssGate.png|250px|thumb|''The Gate within the Abyssal Depths'']]
To open the gate to the maze, players must collect a total of '''25,000 minerals''' within the Abyss.  

The following items are obtainable within the maze:  

; Pan
* Abyssal Pan — $200,000,000,000  

; Shovel
* Abyssal Shovel — $200,000,000,000  

; Equipment Blueprint
* Umbrite Ring

; Rune
* [[Runes|Abyssal Rune]]

=== Maze Solution ===
[[File:Abyss Map.png|thumb|280px|'''The Maze Solution (Credits to @zulisian on discord)''']]

; Umbrite Ring Blueprint
* Enter the Maze until you reach an intersection. Go down the path on the right until you spot another intersection, to which you continue down the path along the grass pathways. There will be a left turn down the path to which you can just ignore as you continue straight until you spot a Skeleton NPC, where you interact to receive the Umbrite Ring Blueprint.

; Abyssal Pan
* Enter the Maze until you reach an intersection. Go down the path on the right until you spot another intersection, to which you continue down the path along the grass pathways. There will be a left turn down the path where you're faced with an obby. Once you're past it, continue down the path to the right, and then take another right, followed by a left, ending up with a right turn until you reach the Abyssal Pan.

; Abyssal Shovel
* Enter the Maze until you reach an intersection. Go down the path on the left until you spot another intersection, to which you can ignore and just go straight until you find a path leading upwards. Climb all the way to the top while continuing on the path until you see a faint glow in the distance, and that's where you'll find the Abyssal Shovel.

=== Tips for the Maze ===
* Carry 10–15 Firefly Flares to keep the path lit.
* Go with another player — the buddy system helps prevent disorientation.
* Drop Firefly Flares at each intersection to mark where you’ve been and keep the darkness from consuming you.
* Find a large Luminum (12–18kg) to provide extra light — it won’t stop the darkness, but it helps visibility.
* Take your time and enjoy exploring the cave!

= Azuralite Oasis =
'''Azuralite Oasis''' is a sub-area of the [[Crystal Caverns]] on [[Mainland]].  
It is the second digsite accessible after {{Crystal Cavern River}}.  

It requires '''Toughness 5''' (at least a '''Divine Shovel''') to dig here.  
There are '''21''' possible [[minerals]].  

== Enchanting ==
At the Azuralite Oasis, players can use the '''Enchanting Table''' to apply [[Enchanting|enchants]] to their shovels.  
Certain enchants require special aetherite types such as '''Iridescent''', '''Voidtorn''', or '''Electric Aetherite'''.  
Some are locked behind the '''Seed of Light Quest'''.  

[[File:Botanist.png|thumb|280px|''The Botanist'']]
== NPCs ==
* [[Botanist]] — quest-giving NPC  

== Minerals ==
; Minerals
* {{Common}} — [[Silver]], [[Copper]], [[Gold]], [[Amethyst]]  
* {{Uncommon}} — [[Neodymium]], [[Smoky Quartz]], [[Malachite]]  
* {{Rare}} — [[Onyx]], [[Azuralite]]

pages.Fungal Marsh: {{Tocright}} [[File:fungalmarsh.png|thumb|280px|''The main area of the Fungal Marsh.'']] = Fungal Marsh = The '''Fungal Marsh''' is a [[Locations|location]] in the Rotwood swamp area. To reach it, go to the town in {{Rotwood Swamp}}, then follow the path in either direction. It contains one main digsite and one sub-location, {{Timelocked Sanctuary}}. You need at least one [[Equipment#tabber-Mythic|Purifying Ring]] to survive, and at least 4 to buy the [[Blightflow Pan]], [[Venomspade Shovel]], or [[Corroded Sluice]]. The [[Events#tabber-Swamp_Fog|Swamp Fog]] event affects the Fungal Marsh, but not its sub-area. == Main Area == === Quest-giving NPCs === * [[Mushroom Man]] - completing his quest awards the [[Blueprint#tabber-Otherworldly_Ring_Blueprint|Otherworldly Ring]] blueprint * [[Froggy]] * [[The Greatest Prospector]] - completing his quest awards the [[Blueprint#tabber-Ring_of_Champions_Blueprint|Ring of Champions]] blueprint === Other Items & Utilities === * [[Blightflow Pan]] * [[Venomspade Shovel]] * [[Corroded Sluice]] * Lever for unlocking the gate to [[Meteor Valley]] * {{Timelocked Sanctuary}} [[Waypoints|Waypoint]] * Annihilation II and Singularity I [[Runes|runes]] * [[Excavations#tabber-Fungal_Marsh|Excavation Site E, "Mysterious Meteor"]] [[File:Rotwoodmap.webp|thumb|300px|''The Rotwood Swamp & Fungal Marsh Map. (Credits to @bs.gabs on discord)'']] [[File:mushroommanarea.png|thumb|280px|''The Mushroom Man'']] [[File:froggythefrog.png|thumb|280px|''Froggy waiting to be fed in the Fungal Marsh'']] === Fungal Marsh Digsite === [[File:fungalmarsharea.png|thumb|280px|''The Fungal Marsh digsite'']] The digsite of {{Fungal Marsh}} requires '''Toughness 7''' (at least a '''Lifetouched Shovel'''). There are '''20''' possible [[minerals]]. ; Minerals * {{Common}} — [[Copper]], [[Gold]] * {{Uncommon}} — [[Titanium]], [[Electrum]], [[Smoky Quartz]], [[Malachite]] * {{Rare}} — [[Onyx]], [[Diopside]] * {{Epic}} — [[Bone]], [[Emerald]], [[Cobalt]], [[Osmium]], [[Mercury]] * {{Legendary}} — [[Diamond]], [[Gloomcap]], [[Bismuth]] * {{Mythic}} — [[Mythril]], [[Red Beryl]], [[Star Garnet]] * {{Exotic}} — [[Astral Spore]] === Toxic Spores === [[File:toxicspores.png|thumb|280px|''The Toxic Spores Warning.'']] * The Toxic Spores are a mist that drains your HP every second whenever you are in the Fungal Marsh area without a [[Equipment#tabber-Mythic|Purifying Ring]] equipped. To prevent the HP loss, simply equip at least one Purifying Ring. * The toxic spores have one advantage: they repel the crocodiles that infest {{Rotwood Swamp}}, so you do not need to worry about being eaten while panning. === Fungal Marsh [[Soundtrack]] === {{Track |location={{Fungal Marsh}} |id=78136740784739 |color=linear-gradient(to right, #aaeecc, #063b38)}} == Timelocked Sanctuary == The sanctuary is a sub-location in the {{Fungal Marsh}}. (Quite literally: it's underground.) * It is open for 30 minutes each hour, from xx:45 to xx:15. * The toxic spores from the Fungal Marsh do ''not'' extend into the sanctuary, but the waypoint is outside, so it ''is'' affected. * [[Events#tabber-Swamp_Fog|Swamp Fog]] also does not affect the sanctuary. === NPCs === * [[File:Timelockedspirit.png|thumb|280px|''The Timelocked Spirit'']] [[Timelocked Spirit]] - completing its quest awards the [[Blueprint#tabber-Timelocked_Soul_Blueprint|Timelocked Soul]] blueprint. * [[Merchant|Timelocked Merchant]] - looks different from other merchants, but serves the same purpose === Other Items & Utilities === * [[Shrines|Timelocked Shrine]] - for extending the time the sanctuary is open * [[Runes|Eternity Rune]] === Timelocked Sanctuary Digsite === Requires '''Toughness 8''' (at least an '''Abyssal Shovel'''). There are '''25''' possible minerals, including 3 {{Exotic}} ones. ; Minerals * {{Common}} — [[Silver]], [[Gold]] * {{Uncommon}} — [[Electrum]], [[Topaz]], [[Smoky Quartz]], [[Malachite]] * {{Rare}} — [[Onyx]], [[Diopside]] * {{Epic}} — [[Glowmoss]], [[Emerald]], [[Cobalt]], [[Osmium]], [[Lightshard]], [[Mercury]] * {{Legendary}} — [[Diamond]], [[Firefly Stone]], [[Starshine]], [[Bismuth]], [[Aetherite]], * {{Mythic}} — [[Red Beryl]], [[Radiant Gold]], [[Star Garnet]], * {{Exotic}} — [[Bloodstone]], [[Astral Spore]], [[Eternium]] === Timelocked Sanctuary [[Soundtrack]] === {{Track |location={{Timelocked Sanctuary}} |id=9046863253 |color=linear-gradient(to right, #3090d0, #48c9b0)}} [[File:Timelocked_sanctuary.png|thumb|280px|''Inside of Timelocked Sanctuary'']] [[Category:Locations]] [[Category:Fungal Marsh]]

= Enchanted Ruins =
'''Enchanted Ruins''' is a sublocation within {{Deeproot Spring}}.  

== Services & NPCs ==
* [[Merchant]] — sell [[Minerals|mineral]]s and [[Equipment|equipment]]
* [[Ruins Archaeologist]] — quest-giving NPC
* [[Ancient Sword]] — quest-giving NPC

=== Extras ===
There is a [[Runes|rune]] hidden along the path from Deeproot Spring to the Enchanted Ruins.

[[File:sword.png|thumb|250px|''An Ancient Sword'']]

== Digsites ==
The ruins require '''Toughness 6'''. There are 23 possible [[Minerals|minerals]].

; Minerals

* {{Mythic}} — [[Radiant Gold]], [[Mythril]], [[Prismara]],
* {{Exotic}} — [[Adamantine]]

[[File:Zrzut ekranu (315).png|thumb|250px|''A Firefly Zone.'']]

== Firefly Zones ==
* '''Firefly Zones''' can spawn here. Digging inside an active zone greatly increases the chances of finding [[Firefly Stone|Firefly Stones]].

== Access ==
If you are coming from the {{Overgrown Grotto}}, go left after entering {{Deeproot Spring}}. If you arrive via the Deeproot Spring [[Waypoints|waypoint]], follow the tunnel down (or jump over the fence).

= Meteor Valley =
'''Meteor Valley''' is a [[Locations|location]] found behind the {{Timelocked Sanctuary}}, near [[The Greatest Prospector]]. 
To gain access, you must first complete the [[Quests#tabber-Timelocked_Sanctuary|Lost in Time]] quest and then pull the lever to open the door.
It contains three main digsites: '''Meteor Falls''', '''Starfall River''', and '''Astral Caverns'''.

== Main Area ==

=== Quest-giving NPCs ===
* [[Valley Girl]]
* [[Familiar Merchant]]
* [[Clockmaker]]
* [[Concussed Resident]]
* [[Valley Golem]]
* [[Astronomer]]
* [[Meteor Wisp]]
* [[Fallen Crate]]
* [[Meteor Guardian]]

=== [[Merchant]] ===
There are three merchants in the valley to help you sell your [[Minerals|minerals]] and [[Equipment|equipment]].
* Meteor Falls: the Shady Merchant is near the Familiar Merchant, across the water from the Entrance portal and waypoint.
* Starfall River: the Merchant is across the river from the [[Astronomer]].
* Astral Caverns: the Merchant is near the [[Alchemist|Alchemist's]] shop.

* [[Waypoints|Waypoint]] — teleportation between locations
* Portal to {{Fungal Marsh}}
* [[Potions#Astral_Caverns_Alchemist|Potion Shop]] — in {{Astral Caverns}}
* Relaxed [[Resident (sitting)|Resident]] — sitting on the shore of {{Starfall River}} near {{Meteor Falls}}
* Standing [[Resident (standing)|Resident]] — near the house at the opposite end of {{Starfall River}}
* [[Nebula Pan]] and [[Starcrusher|Starcrusher Shovel]] can be purchased for $10T each at the house in {{Starfall River}}
* [[Starblossom Sluice]] can be purchased for $25T at the island in the middle of the {{Astral Caverns}} lake
* Annihilation III and Bunny [[Runes]]
* Duplicator [[Trinkets|Trinket]]
* [[Excavations|Excavation Site F (Alien Wreck)]]

{{Tocright}} [[File:Volcanic Sands SWP.png|thumb|280px|''Main area of Caldera Park'']] '''Caldera Park''' is a [[Locations|location]] around and in the Volcano. It is restricted to level 20 and up. [[File:Astral alchemist.png|150px|thumb|''The '''Alchemist''' at their shop in {{Astral Caverns}}.'']]

The '''Alchemist''' is a potion-selling [[NPCs|NPC]] found in multiple regions. 
They sell various [[Potions]] that temporarily boost the player’s [[Stats]].  

Alchemists are one of the primary ways to gain temporary buffs in ''Prospecting!''  

== Gameplay ==
Alchemists allow the player to:
* Purchase [[Potions|potions]] for money or {{Meteor Shards|meteor shards}}  
* Use the potions when purchased, or store them for later use  
* Stack potion durations for extended buffs

== Locations ==

=== Mainland ===
* {{Fortune River Town}} — near the [[Fortune_River#Store|Store]], [[Blacksmith]], and the leaderboards.  

=== Caldera Park ===
* {{Volcanic Sands}} — next to the main village, across the bridge. 

=== Snowy Mountain ===
* {{Frostbitten Path}} — just a little ways down the hill from Frostbite Waterfall.

=== Rotwood Swamp ===
* {{Rotwood Swamp}} — in the middle of the swamp.  

=== Meteor Valley ===
* {{Astral Caverns}} - on the left side of the lake.

[[File:Ancient Ruins (Entrance).png|thumb|280px|''The entrance to the Ancient Ruins'']]

You must unlock the trapdoor with a [[Volcanic Key]] (obtained at the {{Infernal Heart}}) and sacrifice a [[Catseye]], [[Flarebloom]], and [[Uranium]] to enter.  

Inside is a maze containing powerful tools.

=== Maze Solution ===
* '''Shovel & Pan''' — Left, then right, then left. Interact with the bookshelf in the final room to find the '''Fossilized Shovel''' and '''Fossilized Pan'''.
* '''Sluice''' — Turn right three times. Found among barrels is the '''Fossilized Sluice'''.

* Fossilized Shovel — $1,000,000,000  
* Fossilized Pan — $1,000,000,000  
* Fossilized Sluice — $800,000,000

= The Void =
'''The Void''' is a mysterious [[Locations|location]] that appears as a rift in reality.   

=== NPCs and Utilities ===
* [[Interdimensional Traveler]] — quest-giving NPC  
* [[Interdimensional Wanderer]] — dialogue-only NPC  
* Singularity II [[Runes|rune]]

=== Spawning ===
[[File:Void Portal.png|thumb|250px|''The Void Portal'']]  
* The Void can be spawned by a player, using a [[Void Shard]].
* The Void can also be spawned for Robux.
* The Void can spawn during '''Admin Abuse'''.
* When spawned, a portal appears at {{Fortune River}}.

== The Void Digsite ==
The Void digsite's loot pool is unique — it ''changes every time the Void spawns''.  

There is no [[Shovels|shovel]] toughness requirement, and any ore from the game, ''including limited-time ores'' (and except Exotics that aren’t [[Voidstone]]) can appear here. This makes it one of the most unpredictable and lucrative areas.  

The odds for all ores in the same rarity tier are the same, giving the player an opportunity to more easily obtain ores that would otherwise be rarer outside of The Void. The odds for each ore in The Void are shown below.

[[Meteor Shards]] can be obtained commonly from panning, similar to [[Events|Meteor Shower]].

; Minerals  
* {{Common}} — random set of five (changes each spawn) • 18.1132% (~1 in 6) 
* {{Uncommon}} — random set of five (changes each spawn) • 1.8113% (~1 in 55) 
* {{Rare}} — random set of four (changes each spawn) • 0.09057% (~1 in 1,104) 
* {{Epic}} — random set of four (changes each spawn) • 0.003623% (~1 in 27,604) 
* {{Legendary}} — random set of four (changes each spawn) • 0.0001811% (~1 in 552,084) 
* {{Mythic}} — random set of three (changes each spawn) • 0.000002536% (~1 in 39,434,575) 
* {{Exotic}} — [[Voidstone]] • 0.0000007245% (~1 in 138,021,012)  

=== The Gate === 
[[File:Void Gate.png|thumb|250px|''The Gate within the Void'']]  
At the heart of the Void used to lie a gate.  
To open it, players had to collect a total of '''15,000 items''' within the Void.  

Behind the gate, a hidden shop became available:  

; Pan (Unobtainable)
* Galactic Pan — $2,000,000,000  

; Shovel (Unobtainable) 
* Galactic Shovel — $2,000,000,000

'''As of September 13 2025, The Void no longer has this gate.'''

* Any of the plank bridges (but not the tree-trunk bridges). Be careful not to fall off, especially if auto-panning.

pages.Treasure Map:
{{Tocright}}

== Treasure Map ==
A '''Treasure Map''' is a special item you can uncover while digging on various locations around the map. Equipping it guides you to the exact spot where a hidden [[Treasure Chest]] is buried. 

== Overview ==
A Treasure Map is easier to discover when your digspeed is lower. Its base 0.2% drop chance scales inversely to your digspeed. Players can have a maximum of '''5''' Treasure Maps in their inventory at a time. This limit increases to '''10''' with the {{Enchant|Treasure Hunter}} [[Enchanting#tabber-Shovels|shovel enchant]].

[[File:Treasuremap.png|thumb|right|280px|''Equipped Treasure Map'']]

== Obtainment ==
* Dig in any location.
** If you dig in a location that has treasure chests, you have an increased chance of finding that type of map.
* Once a map is found, yellow text will appear on your screen that says "You have found a mysterious map!" 
* Check your inventory (backpack) to see what type of map you found.

== Usage ==
* Head to the location specified on the map.
* Once at the location, click on the map in your inventory to equip it.
* A colored arrow will appear on the screen. Follow the arrow. 
* When you arrive at the correct location, the colored arrow will point at the ground and the text "X Marks the Spot! Dig down!" will appear. 
* When you dig in the location marked by the X, text will appear on the screen that says "You have found buried treasure!!" 
* A [[Treasure Chest]] will appear in your inventory.

=== Troubleshooting ===
* If the arrow points down at a location that is not a deposit, meaning you can't dig there, try digging anywhere in the general vicinity: the hitbox for treasure chests is pretty generous.
* If the arrow keeps going around in circles instead of turning vertical, it might be trying to point at a location that's above you or below you. Try climbing up or down, then checking the map again.
* If, despite your best efforts, you cannot dig up the treasure chest the map is pointing to, '''sell the map''' to a [[Merchant]].
[[File:Tip treasure.png|thumb|center|500px|alt=Tip: Treasure maps can be sold at a merchant if you cannot find their treasure!|Server chat message about recalcitrant treasure maps]]

== Map Types ==
Treasure maps can be obtained anywhere, but they can only point to the following locations:
* {{Fortune River}}
* {{Fortune River Delta}}
* {{Sunset Beach}}
* {{Volcanic Sands}}
* {{Windswept Beach}}
* {{Frostbite River}}
* {{Rotwood Swamp}}
* {{Starfall River}}

[[File:Magma Forge.png|thumb|280px|''The Magma Forge'']]  
A [[Magma Forge|forge]] located at the center of {{Magma Furnace}}.  
It allows players to '''merge two 5★ equipment items''' into '''one 6★ equipment item'''.

=== Infernal Shrine ===
A [[Shrines|shrine]] located in the {{Infernal Heart}} which allows players to extend the time the Heart is open by 30 minutes. It costs {{Meteor Shards|1,000}}, and must be used '''before''' the Heart closes. There is a cooldown period which prevents players from using the shrine frequently.

* [[Waypoints|Waypoint]] — teleportation between locations
* [[Merchant]] — sell [[Minerals|mineral]]s and [[Equipment|equipment]]
* [[Flame Priest]] — quest-giving NPC who allows access to the Magma Furnace
* [[Master of the Forge]] — quest-giving NPC

pages.Seashell Isle:
{{Tocright}} = Seashell Isle = [[File:Seashell Isle Banner.png|500px|center]] '''Seashell Isle''' is the [[Locations|location]] of the Summer Event. It is a moving island that floats around on its own, and is only close enough to the mainland to sail to in the summer. == Getting There == To get to Seashell Isle, talk to the [[Ferryman]] at the {{Fortune River}} dock during the Summer Event. == Shops == === Blueprint and Trinket Vendor === [[File:Summer Relic Vendor.png|border|250px|The blueprint and trinket vendor's stall]]
This [[Blueprint_%26_Trinket_Vendor|vendor]] sells two blueprints and one trinket. * [[Blueprint#tabber-Waverider_Blueprint|Waverider Blueprint]] – {{Sand Dollars|1000}} (stock: 1) * [[Blueprint#tabber-Shell_Necklace_Blueprint|Shell Necklace Blueprint]] – {{Sand Dollars|500}} (stock: 1) * [[Trinkets|Beach Umbrella (Trinket)]] – {{Sand Dollars|1000}} === Relic Vendor === [[File:Summer Blueprint Vendor.png|border|250px|The relic vendor's stall]]
This [[Relic_Vendor|vendor]] sells a limited stock of five [[Relics|relics]]. * {{Meteor Fragment}} – {{Sand Dollars|300}} (stock: 1) * {{Void Shard}} – {{Sand Dollars|300}} (stock: 1) * {{Infernal Idol}} – {{Sand Dollars|50}} (stock: 5) * {{Solar Magnifier}} – {{Sand Dollars|40}} (stock: 25) * {{Friendship Totem}} – {{Sand Dollars|40}} (stock: 50 per day) === Bonfire Shop === [[File:Summer_XPCookie.png|border|200px|XP cookie near the Bonfire]]
Up to 200 {{XP Cookie}}s can be purchased per day for {{Sand Dollars|20}} each from a spot next to the Bonfire. == Quest-giving NPCs == * [[Photographer]] * [[Drake]] * [[Vagrant]] == Other NPCs & Utilities == * [[Merchant]] — allows selling of [[minerals]] and [[Equipment|equipment]] * [[Waypoints|Waypoint]] — fast travel to other locations * [[Island Guide]] — information-giving NPC * [[Ferryman]] — travel back to {{Fortune River}} * [[Beachgoer]] * [[Surfer]] * [[Resident]] * [[Trader]] - see '''Summer Collection''' below == Unique Features == === Summer Collection === [[File:Summer Collection.png|thumb|Empty crates, waiting to be filled]] Submit 10 ores with the Summer, Tidal, or Hearthflame [[Modifiers|modifiers]] to the crates next to the [[Trader]]. Wait 1 hour for them to be delivered, and then claim rewards including [[Relics|relics]] and {{Sand Dollars|Sand Dollars}}. The quality of the delivery depends on the ore rarities and modifiers. The weight of the ores doesn't matter. {| class="wikitable" |- ! Delivery Quality ! Summer ! Tidal ! Hearthflame |- ! {{Common}} | 2% || 4% || 5% |- ! {{Uncommon}} | 3% || 6% || 7.5% |- ! {{Rare}} | 5% || 10% || 12.5% |- ! {{Epic}} | 8% || 16% || 20% |- ! {{Legendary}} | 12% || 24% || 30% |- ! {{Mythic}} | 25% || 50% || 62.5% |- ! {{Exotic}} | 50% || 100% || 125% |} === Bonfire === [[File:Bonfire - in progress.png|200px|border|Sand Dollar collection in progress]] [[File:Bonfire - active.png|200px|border|Goal reached!]]
Whenever the global Sand Dollar collection goal is reached, the bonfire in the center of Seashell Isle lights up, starting a random [[Events|event]]. All methods of Sand Dollar acquisition count towards the goal - finding them on beaches and deposits, getting them from the Summer Collection, and completing quests. The Bonfire randomly selects one of these events: * [[Events#tabber-Night_of_the_Bonfire_-_Limited|Night of the Bonfire]] * [[Events#tabber-Meteor_Shower|Meteor Shower]] * [[Events#tabber-4×_Luck|4× Luck]] * [[Events#tabber-8×_Luck|8× Luck]] ==== Extending the Bonfire ==== If players collect sufficient {{Sand Dollars|Sand Dollars}} '''while the Bonfire is lit''', the event currently running (Meteor Shower, Night of the Bonfire, 4× Luck, ''or'' 8× Luck) is extended by 15 minutes. The goal to be reached is shown above the Bonfire while it is lit. === ''Shifting Tides'' Hourly Event === [[File:Shifting tides at Windswept beach.png|300px|right]] The '''Shifting Tides''' event happens every hour at XX:05 and lasts '''15 minutes'''. It gives a +1× {{Stat|Luck}} Boost to all locations, and gives a chance of the [[Modifiers#Tidal|Tidal modifier]] on ores collected at beach deposits. * Beach deposits will have large swirling circles, but it is not necessary to dig/pan in those circles - the Tidal modifier chance applies to the whole deposit. == Digsite == '''Seashell Beach''' is the only digsite in this event location. The toughness requirement is 1, so any [[Shovels|shovel]] will work.
